edits.name: Operator self-checks: a daily Google sign-in check, with audits and drills run by Tony
edits.description: One daily check on the Mac tells Tony, and only Tony, when a Google sign-in that Happy's mail reading depends on has stopped working, so an expired sign-in does not first show up as a missing or empty morning text. The security audit (after every update and each month), the monthly checklist and the quarterly restore drill and key rotation stay commands Tony runs himself, prompted by reminders on his own calendar. Behaviour test cases join the existing eval suite when the feature they test ships, and are run on demand and after a critical-path change, as already decided.
edits.example: Trigger: the stored Google sign-in for Tony's Gmail stops working. Within a day the check raises an alert on Tony's phone through ntfy, the route his other alerts use, and nothing is sent to the family. He renews the sign-in and the next run is clean.
edits.how: Daily: a launchd job runs one small read-only script as the happy user, as the sandbox check and the eval job in the config repo already do. It runs `gog auth list --check` and reads every entry reported, because the exit status alone does not prove each stored sign-in is valid, then reports as those checks do: one ok-or-not metric for a Grafana rule, or a counts-only line to ntfy. No OpenClaw scheduler job, no model call, no text from Happy. Not jobs: the security audit after every update and each month, the monthly checklist (spend caps, new stores in the backup, standing approvals) and the quarterly restore drill and key rotation are calendar reminders for Tony, who runs them himself; the audit and doctor commands already exist in happy-inspect. Behaviour cases: each feature adds its own case to the existing eval set when it ships; no fixtures are built ahead.
depends_on: gog installed on the Mac mini and at least one Google sign-in stored (wave A's sign-in phase, with the mail card G015)
The alert route that exists since M1: VictoriaMetrics, Grafana rules and ntfy

caveats: The five-minute dead-man probe and the M1 Grafana alerts already cover 'gateway down' and 'iMessage unhealthy'. The only new signal here is the Google sign-in; do not build the same alert twice.
The check cannot run until gog is installed and a sign-in is stored; gog is not on the Mac mini today.

Given up with this form: a daily look at the model sign-in, the channel probe and plugin load state (Tony looks at plugin load state after each deploy instead), automatic comparison of audit results between runs, and results arriving in the iMessage thread.

The monthly and quarterly items are reminder lines, not a feature: spend caps, the daily budget alert and the nightly verified backup already exist. The backup archive holds sign-ins and keys unencrypted and must never be copied to iCloud.
Plain doctor can migrate state, so the by-hand checks use its lint form, as happy-inspect already does.

Behaviour cases run the real model and cost tokens on every run, and the daily cost alert does not see eval-clone spend; eval clones must keep messaging tools denied, or a reminder test would text the family.
edits.safety: The check is read-only and runs on the host: no agent gains exec or any other tool, no model reads its output, and the result goes only to Tony, as a count or an ok-or-not signal with no mail content. Behaviour cases added later call the model only against eval clones with fake users and fake secrets.
